source.title: Removing Information Content Does Not Certify Tamper Resistance in Open-Weight Models
source.authors: Domenic Rosati; Alessa Carbo; Ali Dadsetan; Hong Huang; Matthew Young; Subhabrata Majumdar; Frank Rudzicz; Hassan Sajjad

record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery after fine-tuning filtered and unfiltered safety-related checkpoints, and argues that their apparent recovery-speed gap can be erased or reversed by function-preserving reparameterization. Its measured outcome is WMDP-bio task accuracy, not refusal or harmful-request compliance as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The Deep Ignorance experiment reports full-model fine-tuning on WMDP-bio and records training accuracy, held-out accuracy, and time to a training-accuracy threshold. These results concern recovery on a harmful-domain benchmark, but do not measure refusal or user-directed harmful-request compliance, so they are recorded under versions ["none"]. Other experiments on AG News, E2E-NLG, synthetic tasks, and non-harmful target classes do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study cites Qi et al. (2023) only as motivation. Its experiments measure fine-tuning recovery of WMDP-bio multiple-choice accuracy on pretraining-filtered Deep Ignorance base checkpoints, plus toy and Pythia/BERT tasks. These are capability-relearning measures on models that are not refusal-trained. None of the experiments measures harmful-request compliance, refusal, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypass, safety-localized parameters, or deepening training. The reader's 'tests/T5' contradicts its own finding that every row bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that mutual information at release cannot alone certify slow fine-tuning recovery, and that guarantees must constrain attack dynamics. They also claim more strongly that the Deep Ignorance tamper-resistance results look like parameterization artifacts, so safety pretraining may add little tamper resistance. They caveat that this holds for their runs and budget.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines mutual-information conditions and function-preserving reparameterization effects on fine-tuning recovery, rather than the original papers’ refusal, token-KL, or compliant-prefill tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery outcomes vary with Q/K rescaling: SF at α = 8 reaches a similar final training accuracy to UF at α = 1, while UF at α = 1/24 has slower median threshold attainment and lower final accuracy than UF at α = 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Function-preserving Q/K rescaling erases or reverses the WMDP-bio recovery gap between Deep Ignorance strong-filter and unfiltered checkpoints. SF at α=8 reaches 69.3% training accuracy vs UF at α=1's 68.9%. UF at α=1/24 slows to 225 updates vs SF's 150.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured tamper resistance (fine-tuning recovery speed) of pretraining-filtered models depends on parameterization, so recovery gaps cannot be attributed solely to removed information.

record.code_released: Code and data to be released upon publication.
record.problems: The WMDP-bio experiment uses three seeds and reports task accuracy rather than refusal or harmful-request compliance. Consequently it does not directly establish any of the listed behavior-specific versions. The paper notes that the demonstrated recovery ranking concerns these runs and budget; full-model fine-tuning is needed for the Q/K symmetry to alter attack optimization geometry.
record.rows_left_out: The Pythia-160M AG News and E2E-NLG order experiments, mathematical toy constructions, Fashion-MNIST and Pythia-14M orbit demonstrations, and BERT-Tiny AG News scrub/orbit results were omitted because they do not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance, first-token KL, or another behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate after harmful fine-tuning; WMDP-bio accuracy relearning on non-refusal-trained base models only.
No benign fine-tuning effect on safety.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks; the Q/K rescaling concerns optimization geometry.
No analysis of why safety alignment is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: The study concerns tamper resistance of data-filtered base models and capability relearning, not shallow refusal alignment. Relation was corrected from tests/T5 to cites_only/T6, since every row's link is 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal or harmful-request compliance rate is measured; WMDP-bio multiple-choice accuracy is not the specified behavior.
No benign-data fine-tuning effect on harmful-request refusal or compliance is measured.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes are tested for refusal bypass.
The study analyzes parameterization-dependent optimization geometry, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study does not test whether safety-training data or objectives cause first-token shallowness.
No training to spread safety beyond initial response tokens is tested.
